phrases.english: I was trying to say that you speak it very well
phrases.other: o'n i'n trio deud bo' ti'n siarad hi yn dda iawn
phrases.qa_notes: Natural conversational English and excellent colloquial North Welsh. 'trio deud' and 'bo' ti'n' are authentic spoken forms. Pedagogically valuable - complex embedded clause.

phrases.english: how to say something
phrases.other: sut i ddeud rhywbeth
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but useful - common pattern. Welsh is grammatically correct with soft mutation after 'i'. Good building block.

phrases.english: the old woman
phrases.other: yr hen ddynas
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect. 'ddynas' is authentically North Welsh (vs 'ddynes'/'fenyw'). Correct soft mutation after 'hen'. Natural both languages.

phrases.english: but I'm not sure if I can remember anything else
phrases.other: ond dw i ddim yn siwr os medra i gofio unrhywbeth arall
phrases.qa_notes: Natural conversational phrase in both languages. 'medra i' is good North Welsh form. Long but realistic.

phrases.english: he doesn't want to talk to me until next week
phrases.other: dydy o ddim isio siarad efo fi tan wythnos nesa'
phrases.qa_notes: Excellent. 'isio' and 'efo' are distinctly North Welsh. 'wythnos nesa' natural. Both sides flow well.

phrases.english: I'll see you there
phrases.other: wela i chdi yno
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect everyday phrase. 'chdi' is distinctly North Welsh. Natural in both languages. High frequency usage.

phrases.english: I can't try
phrases.other: fedra i ddim trio
phrases.qa_notes: Welsh is grammatically correct ('fedra' North form, soft mutation). English is slightly awkward - people rarely say this exact phrase. More natural: 'I can't even try'.

phrases.english: if you knew what was happening
phrases.other: 'set ti'n gwybod be' oedd yn digwydd
phrases.qa_notes: Excellent conditional clause. ''set ti'n' is authentic North Welsh contraction (tasai/baset). Good pedagogical value for conditionals.

phrases.english: I'd tell you if I could help you
phrases.other: byddwn i'n deu' 'tho ti 'swn i'n medru helpu chdi
phrases.qa_notes: Complex conditional. Welsh shows authentic contractions ('deu' 'tho', ''swn i'n'). English is functional but slightly unusual word order - more natural: 'If I could help you, I'd tell you'.

phrases.english: he wanted to tell me
phrases.other: oedd o isio deud wrthaf fi
phrases.qa_notes: Welsh is correct but 'wrthaf fi' is slightly formal/redundant - 'wrtha i' more common in speech. English natural.

phrases.english: I'd try to help you if you'd slow down
phrases.other: mi driwn i helpu chdi 'sech chdi'n arafu
phrases.qa_notes: Good conditional structure. 'mi driwn i' is authentic North Welsh. ''sech chdi'n' correct conditional. Both languages natural.

phrases.english: is that they're not serious
phrases.other: ydy nad ydyn nhw ddim o ddifri'
phrases.qa_notes: ISSUE: English is a fragment that sounds incomplete - missing context. Welsh construction 'ydy nad ydyn nhw ddim' is grammatically complex but natural in full context. As standalone, awkward in English.

phrases.english: I was speaking with my brother yesterday
phrases.other: o'n i'n siarad efo fy mrawd ddoe
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect. Natural in both languages. Correct nasal mutation 'mrawd'. 'efo' distinctly North Welsh. Common real-world usage.

phrases.english: I'd like to give it to him now
phrases.other: liciwn i roi fo iddo fo rwan
phrases.qa_notes: Natural in both. 'liciwn i' good North form. 'iddo fo' correct. Practical everyday phrase.

phrases.english: the young boy
phrases.other: yr hogyn ifanc
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect. 'hogyn' is distinctly North Welsh (vs 'bachgen' in South). Natural and simple.

phrases.english: you've learnt to speak
phrases.other: ti 'di dysgu siarad
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but useful building block. Welsh contracted form 'ti 'di' is authentic spoken Welsh. Slightly incomplete in English but pedagogically useful.

phrases.english: I wouldn't give him more time
phrases.other: fyddwn i ddim yn rhoi mwy o amser iddo fo
phrases.qa_notes: Natural conditional negative. Welsh structure correct. Both sound like real speech.

phrases.english: to speak Welsh very well
phrases.other: siarad Cymraeg yn dda iawn
phrases.qa_notes: Infinitive fragment but very useful. Welsh correct. Common phrase learners need.

phrases.english: she wants to know what you said
phrases.other: mae hi isio gwybod be' ddudest ti
phrases.qa_notes: Excellent. Natural in both. 'isio' North form. 'ddudest' correct soft mutation. Useful embedded question structure.

phrases.english: you're doing something very well now
phrases.other: ti'n gwneud rhywbeth yn dda iawn rwan
phrases.qa_notes: Functional and correct. English slightly vague ('something') but could be natural encouragement. Welsh correct.

phrases.english: could you say it more slowly, because it's interesting?
phrases.other: fedri di ddeud o yn arafach, achos mae'n ddiddorol?
phrases.qa_notes: Welsh perfect with 'fedri di' (North), correct mutations. English slightly unusual combination - asking to slow down because interesting is a bit odd, but plausible.

phrases.english: I thought it was fairly good
phrases.other: o'n i'n meddwl bo' hi'n eitha' da
phrases.qa_notes: Natural in both languages. Good use of 'eitha' (fairly/quite). Authentic conversational register.

phrases.english: next Friday
phrases.other: dydd Gwener nesa'
phrases.qa_notes: Simple and essential. 'nesa' correct contracted form. High utility phrase.

phrases.english: do you feel like doing something to help before you go?
phrases.other: wyt ti'n teimlo fel gwneud rhywbeth i helpu cyn i ti fynd?
phrases.qa_notes: Natural question in both languages. Welsh structure correct with 'cyn i ti fynd'. Good complex sentence practice.

phrases.english: my brother said
phrases.other: ddudodd fy mrawd
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but useful. 'ddudodd' North form (vs 'dwedodd'). Correct nasal mutation on 'mrawd'.

phrases.english: do you want to speak slowly?
phrases.other: wyt ti isio siarad yn araf?
phrases.qa_notes: Welsh correct. English slightly awkward - more natural to ask 'do you want ME to speak slowly?' or 'can you speak more slowly?' Current form implies asking if they PREFER speaking slowly.

phrases.english: he didn't tell me what she wanted
phrases.other: wnaeth o'm deud wrthaf fi be' oedd hi isio
phrases.qa_notes: Good complex sentence. 'wnaeth o'm' authentic contraction. 'wrthaf fi' slightly formal but acceptable. Both natural.

phrases.english: I don't want to talk about it at the moment
phrases.other: dw i'm isio siarad amdani ar hyn o bryd
phrases.qa_notes: Excellent. Natural in both languages. 'dw i'm isio' authentic contraction. 'ar hyn o bryd' good idiomatic phrase.

phrases.english: yes, I watched it last night
phrases.other: do, wnes i ei gwylio hi neithiwr
phrases.qa_notes: Natural conversational response. 'do' as affirmative to past question is correct. 'ei gwylio hi' shows object pronoun structure.

phrases.english: I met someone in the restaurant who said that he knows the old man
phrases.other: wnes i gyfarfod rhywun yn y ty bwyta ddudodd fod o'n nabod yr hen ddyn
phrases.qa_notes: Complex relative clause - excellent pedagogical value. Natural in both. 'ty bwyta' common, 'ddudodd' North form.

phrases.english: I'm trying to say
phrases.other: dw i'n trio deud
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but useful. Welsh authentic spoken form. Good building block for longer sentences.

phrases.english: I didn't do a lot on Sunday afternoon but it was nice to watch a bit of television
phrases.other: wnes i ddim gwneud llawer bnawn dydd Sul ond oedd yn braf gwylio bach o deledu
phrases.qa_notes: Long but natural narrative. 'bnawn dydd Sul' authentic time expression. 'bach o deledu' colloquial. Good conversational practice.

phrases.english: someone who said that she knows
phrases.other: rhywun ddudodd bod hi'n nabod
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment - needs object in English. Welsh structure correct but incomplete. Useful for building but awkward standalone.

phrases.english: can you tell me what you want to do?
phrases.other: fedri di ddeud wrtha i be' ti isio gwneud?
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect. Natural question in both languages. 'fedri di' North form. Embedded question well constructed.

phrases.english: do you like that?
phrases.other: wyt ti'n licio hynna?
phrases.qa_notes: Simple and essential. 'licio' common informal form. 'hynna' correct demonstrative. High utility.

phrases.english: he didn't tell me how to do it
phrases.other: wnaeth o'm deud wrthaf fi sut i wneud o
phrases.qa_notes: Good sentence. 'wnaeth o'm' authentic contraction. 'wrthaf fi' slightly formal - 'wrtha i' more colloquial but acceptable.

phrases.english: I've still got to improve
phrases.other: mae dal rhaid i mi wella
phrases.qa_notes: Natural self-deprecating statement. 'dal rhaid' good colloquial construction. Minor: 'wella' soft mutation correct.

phrases.english: the young woman said
phrases.other: ddudodd y ddynas ifanc
phrases.qa_notes: Fragment but useful for reported speech. 'ddynas' North form. Mutations correct.

phrases.english: she said that she was too busy to help me do it
phrases.other: ddudodd hi bo' hi'n rhy brysur i helpu fi wneud o
phrases.qa_notes: Complex reported speech. Natural in both. 'bo' hi'n' authentic contraction. Good pedagogical value.

phrases.english: would you like to tell me?
phrases.other: fyddet ti'n licio deud wrthaf fi?
phrases.qa_notes: Polite request form. Welsh conditional 'fyddet ti'n' correct. 'wrthaf fi' slightly formal but acceptable.

phrases.english: in the restaurant yesterday
phrases.other: yn y ty bwyta ddoe
phrases.qa_notes: Simple locative phrase. Fragment but useful building block. 'ty bwyta' (eating house) natural North Welsh.

phrases.english: don't take too much of a risk
phrases.other: paid a chymryd gormod o risg
phrases.qa_notes: Good imperative negative. 'paid a' + aspirate mutation on 'cymryd'. Natural advice in both languages.

phrases.english: you'd tell me, wouldn't you?
phrases.other: byddet ti'n deu' 'tha fi, fysat ti?
phrases.qa_notes: Tag question structure. Welsh shows authentic contractions. 'fysat ti' correct tag form. Natural conversational tone.

phrases.english: I met someone in the restaurant last night who said that he knows
phrases.other: wnes i gyfarfod rhywun yn y ty bwyta neithiwr ddudodd fod o'n nabod
phrases.qa_notes: English incomplete - 'who said that he knows' what/whom? Welsh same issue. Fragment from larger context but odd standalone.

phrases.english: I'd better say that I've been learning Welsh
phrases.other: well i mi ddeud bo' fi wedi bod yn dysgu Cymraeg
phrases.qa_notes: Natural self-introduction phrase. 'well i mi' correct Welsh idiom for 'I'd better'. Very useful for learners.

phrases.english: I started about a week ago
phrases.other: wnes i ddechrau tua wythnos yn ol
phrases.qa_notes: Natural time expression. Both languages perfectly natural. Good conversational phrase.

phrases.english: can I get you anything?
phrases.other: ga i nol unrhywbeth i chi?
phrases.qa_notes: Perfect hospitality phrase. 'ga i nol' natural offer form. 'i chi' shows politeness register. High utility.

phrases.english: someone who knows that you want to read that book
phrases.other: rhywun sy'n gwybod bo' ti isio darllen y llyfr 'na
phrases.qa_notes: Complex relative clause. Welsh structure correct. English natural. Good practice for embedded clauses.

phrases.english: how to try
phrases.other: sut i drio
phrases.qa_notes: Minimal fragment. Welsh correct with soft mutation on 'trio'. English sparse but pedagogically useful as building block. Not standalone natural.

phrases.english: do you want me to help you?
phrases.other: wyt ti isio i mi helpu chdi?
phrases.qa_notes: Natural offer of help. Welsh structure 'isio i mi' correct. 'chdi' North form. High utility phrase.
